stories.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
stories.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.
stories.explanation: A flaw in PHP (the software that powers about 70% of websites) lets attackers take complete control of affected servers, which is why you're seeing lots of 404 errors as sites go down or get shut down preemptively. This matters because it's widespread—affecting millions of websites—and attackers already have working attack code. Defenders need to update PHP immediately to patched versions and monitor their systems for signs of compromise.

stories.title: PHP ships emergency patches for critical PHP2Shell flaws
stories.summary: The PHP security team released emergency security patches for two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell.
stories.explanation: PHP released emergency security patches for two critical vulnerabilities (PHP2Shell) that allow remote code execution (RCE, meaning running unauthorized commands on a server) without needing login credentials. This matters because the flaws are in the core language itself, affecting a huge portion of the internet, and updates are emergency-only because exploits are actively being used. Defenders must apply patches to all affected PHP versions as their highest priority.

stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
stories.summary: Microsoft on Wednesday disclosed that a China state-aligned actor dubbed Storm-0940 was behind the recent supply chain compromise of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application. During the incident, Storm-0940 used ARTEX, a Go-based agentic AI penetration testing framework that was made closed-source in the wake of its abuse in cyber attacks targeting South Korean financial institutions, to speed
stories.explanation: A Chinese state-backed hacking group compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup software in the supply chain (meaning the attacker broke into the vendor's systems, not individual customers' networks) and used an AI-based penetration testing tool called ARTEX to move through victim networks. This matters because supply chain attacks affect thousands of organizations at once, and the use of AI tools shows sophisticated attacker capabilities. Defenders need to patch ConnectWise immediately, hunt for unauthorized access in their systems, and monitor for the specific tools this group is known to use.

stories.title: PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge
stories.summary: PHP has released emergency updates that fix two critical flaws in the language itself, letting an attacker without an account run code on a web server. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the PHP team says only updating fully protects a server. The flaws, together called PHP2Shell, sit in the PHP runtime, not in any application, so a site is exposed even when its own
stories.explanation: PHP released emergency security updates fixing two critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers run commands on web servers without any account access—the fixes are available in specific patched versions (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35). This matters because it's a core language vulnerability affecting millions of sites, and partial patches don't help. Defenders must update to the full patched versions and verify the update actually took effect.

stories.title: CISA: SafePay ransomware hit over 600 critical infrastructure orgs
stories.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) says the SafePay ransomware gang has breached over 600 critical infrastructure organizations worldwide since 2024.
stories.explanation: The SafePay ransomware gang has attacked and successfully encrypted data on over 600 critical infrastructure organizations (power plants, hospitals, utilities, etc.) since 2024, according to CISA (a U.S. government cybersecurity agency). This matters because critical infrastructure attacks can endanger public safety and national security, and 600 breaches means this group is highly active and successful. Defenders in critical infrastructure must assume they're a target, enforce strong backup strategies, and implement detection tools specifically tuned for ransomware.

stories.title: Critical GitLab Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Could Allow Unauthenticated RCE Across 12 Years of Releases
stories.summary: GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014. The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the October 12 update covered only versions 19.2 and later, and the new fixed versions sit one patch above it, so an
stories.explanation: GitLab released a patch for a flaw (rated 10.0, the highest severity) that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed GitLab servers, and the flaw exists in every version released since 2014—even organizations that patched 9 days earlier are still vulnerable. This matters because GitLab is used by many organizations to store and manage code, so a breach can compromise source code and secrets, and the wide affected range means almost all GitLab users need to patch immediately. Defenders must apply the October 21 patch regardless of previous patch dates and scan server logs for suspicious activity.

stories.title: Authorities disrupt nearly 11,000 cybercrime networks in Africa
stories.summary: Law enforcement agencies have disrupted nearly 11,000 cybercriminal networks and arrested more than 1,400 people in Operation Serengeti III, which targeted business email compromise, ransomware, and online scams.
stories.explanation: Law enforcement agencies worldwide arrested over 1,400 cybercriminals and shut down nearly 11,000 criminal networks in Operation Serengeti III, targeting business email compromise scams, ransomware gangs, and online fraud. This matters because it shows that coordinated law enforcement action can disrupt criminal operations at scale. Defenders should use this window to strengthen defenses against these attack types, knowing that some of the criminals behind recent attacks are now arrested or displaced.

stories.title: LiteLLM Suspects GitHub Token Leak in AI Gateway Logs Behind Malicious Package Release
stories.summary: LiteLLM on Wednesday disclosed that threat actors compromised "multiple independent security controls" to push a malicious version of the Python package containing a credential stealer and a backdoor. On October 21, 2026, LiteLLM's release pipeline was compromised to push 1.107.0 to the Docker Hub registry and the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository. The incident took place around 4:00 a.m.
stories.explanation: Attackers compromised LiteLLM's code release system and pushed a malicious version of their Python software package that included a credential stealer and backdoor; the compromise suggests attackers leaked stolen GitHub tokens (security credentials) from system logs to gain access. This matters because Python packages are widely downloaded and trusted, so a compromised package can infect thousands of developer machines and systems, and it shows that logging systems can leak secrets if not properly protected. Defenders need to audit their Python package versions, rotate any GitHub credentials, and implement secret detection in logs.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2015-5477 is a vulnerability in ISC BIND (the software that translates domain names to IP addresses) where improper data processing allows attackers to cause problems with DNS services. This matters because DNS is foundational to the internet, so disruptions affect all web services. Defenders should ensure BIND is patched and monitor for unusual DNS query patterns.

cves.explanation: CVE-2015-3306 is an access control flaw in ProFTPD (file transfer software) that lets users access files they shouldn't have permission to reach. This matters because file servers often hold sensitive company data. Defenders need to update ProFTPD and audit who has accessed which files.

cves.explanation: CVE-2016-3081 is a command injection flaw in Apache Struts (web development framework) where attackers can run arbitrary commands by exploiting how the framework processes user input. Defenders must patch Struts and review web application logs for suspicious commands.

cves.explanation: CVE-2026-104935 is an authentication bypass flaw in Ivanti Connect Secure (remote access software) where attackers can trick the system into granting access by spoofing identity, allowing them to bypass login. This matters because remote access software is a primary target—a breach means attackers can enter corporate networks without credentials. Defenders need to patch immediately and add additional authentication checks (like requiring a second factor).

This matters because document servers hold confidential company files. Defenders must patch ONLYOFFICE and audit logs for attempted path traversal attacks.
